messages:
jia: FYI perf regression after the kernel-selection tweak landed on canary at 11:40. ~8-12% extra host CPU on small requests, latency tail up ~20ms. attaching quick notes and traces.

sam: ouch. any obvious hotspot?

jia: pprof top shows a jump in host-side parsing + grpc write path. stack samples cluster in parse_buffer -> tokenize_run -> writev_coalesce.

morgan: do you have the flamegraph?

jia: uploaded: https://internal.gists/reports/2938475610/flame.svg (redwood-internal link) 

jia: paste of the abbreviated perf top:
```
Samples: 2.3k of 30.0k (7.67%)  command: runtime-server
   28.5%  runtime-server  [.] parse_buffer
   16.2%  runtime-server  [.] grpc::Writev
   11.0%  runtime-server  [.] tokenize_run
    6.5%  runtime-server  [.] kvcache::lookup
    4.0%  runtime-server  [.] http2::frame_unwrap
```

ashley: kvcache shows a slight increase too. could be more churn because tokenization now emits different framing?

jia: hypothesis: kernel selector change prefers a variant that increases host preproc (more small frames) so grpc writev can't coalesce as efficiently -> more write syscalls and CPU. also tokenization path now splits slightly earlier so we do extra UTF-8 checks on host.

morgan: can we repro locally with the same canary config? useful to run tcpdump + strace on the proxy to see write syscall pattern.

jia: repro script: `./tools/bench -c ./configs/canary-0932.yaml --qps 200 --payload small`

jia: strace snippet (write syscalls):
```
write(3, "\x00\x01...", 256) = 256
write(3, "\x00\x01...", 128) = 128
write(3, "\x00\x01...", 64) = 64
```

morgan: those small writes match the hypothesis. ops-bot, did we roll any proxy config that changed TCP_NODELAY or writev coalesce on canary pool?

ops-bot: Canary pool config updated 2026-03-20 11:37 by deploy-bot: `enable_writev_coalesce=false` for kernel-variant b.

sam: aha. why was coalesce disabled?

ops-bot: change note: experiment to measure per-request jitter when coalescing caused request-level head-of-line in a microbenchmark. flagged by perf team.

ashley: so two things: kernel selector picks variant b more often, and coalesce is off -> more syscalls + parse work. both compatible with the regress.

jia: quick mitigation: re-enable writev coalesce on canary and run a/b vs kernel selector fork. also plan to queue a microfix to delay token-split until after writev aggregation in the proxy.

morgan: before reverting, can we test a toggle that keeps kernel selector but flips coalesce=true? if that recovers baseline we narrow blame.

jia: ran that: coalesce=true returned CPU to within 1-2% of baseline and tail latency improved. link to postmortem notes: https://internal.docs/infra/2938475610/coalesce-toggle.md

sam: nice. does kvcache still matter?

jia: kvcache hitrate unchanged, but lookup CPU rose because parse path now issues extra small lookups per request (token boundaries changed). batching heuristic should collapse those lookups into a single multi-get.

ashley: can we add a cheap collapse in host proxy as a stopgap: buffer token ids for 1ms and issue combined lookup? low risk and should reduce lookup calls for chatty small prompts.

jia: prototype patch attached in PR 7891. microbench shows ~6% CPU drop on host parse, end-to-end latency tail down ~12ms.

morgan: schedule: rollback coalesce=false from canary now, merge the collapse patch behind a feature flag, run canary smoke, then re-evaluate kernel selector rollout.

sam: agree. also add a perf test that compares kernel variants with coalesce toggled so we avoid future surprises.

jia: created perf test: `perf/host-tokenflow/coalesce-kernel-comparison` and added to nightly.

perf-bot: nightly perf run enqueued: perf/host-tokenflow/coalesce-kernel-comparison @ 02:00 UTC.

morgan: one more ask — add a p99 write syscall histogram to ingress dashboard (per-proxy) so we can see small-write storms in future.

ashley: will add chart. also adding a small audit to rollout checklist: "verify writev_coalesce setting compatibility with kernel selector".

jia: thanks all — rolling canary coalesce=true now and watching. will post results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
